validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + CLASSIFICATION + ROUTE, checked independently of GEM/wiki. The sheet's own wiki page cites energybase.ru (backlinks=8, i.e. the source most of the page's facts trace to) and a Wikipedia article; I engaged both before open search. energybase.ru's own object page (fetched via r.jina.ai reader after our network's direct IP was blocked by the site's own bot-wall — curl and url_verifier both get energybase's 'access restricted / your IP is blocked' page, HTTP 200, so the URL FAILS url_verifier and is NOT proposed as a ref) lists: 'Газопровод Елец - Кременчуг - Кривой Рог' operated by ООО «Газпром трансгаз Москва» (a Gazprom subsidiary), Диаметр труб 1420 мм, год ввода 1986, and lists this pipeline as one of three trunks passing through compressor station КС Долгое alongside Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod and Yamburg-Progress — i.e. it sits in the same Russian southern-corridor cluster as those two GEM rows, geographically plausible and internally consistent. Wikipedia's 'Natural gas in Ukraine' article (merged from 'Natural gas transmission system of Ukraine', verified OK on tokens 'Kryvyi Rih'+'Sudzha', '1986'+'Yelets', and 'southern transit corridor'+'Yelets') independently states: 'Main pipelines of the southern transit corridor are the Yelets–Kremenchuk–Kryvyi Rih pipeline...' and 'Between 1986 and 2001, the Yelets–Kremenchuk–Ananyiv–Tiraspol–Izmail route was developed', and 'The Yelets–Kremenchuk–Kryvyi Rih pipeline enters into Ukraine through the Sudzha gas metering station.' All of this is cited to a named, dated, checkable primary document: Naftogaz / Energy Charter Secretariat, 'Master Plan. Ukrainian Gas Transmission System (UGTS). Priority Objects. Modernisation and Reconstruction' (2009), http://www.energycharter.org/fileadmin/DocumentsMedia/Presentations/CBP-Ukraine_GTS.pdf. I downloaded and read that PDF directly (it is live, 3.1MB, 19 pages) with pdftotext -layout: it explicitly lists 'Elets-Kremenchuk-Kryvyi Rig' as one of the two named lines of the 'South transit corridor' (the other being Ananiiv-Tyraspol-Izmail), entering via Sudzha, and dedicates a slide ('Modernisation and Reconstruction of South Transit Corridor: Elets-Kremenchuk-Kryvyi Rig / Ananiiv-Tyraspol-Izmail', finance expenditure $366.3 mln USD) to this exact pipeline — confirming the wiki citation actually names this pipeline (not a generic aggregate cite). url_verifier FAILs on this PDF for specific-digit tokens ('323', '1420') — a known large-PDF extraction-depth limitation documented in url_verifier.py's own docstring (the OPEC ASB2012 case); I manually confirmed via pdftotext -layout that 'Elets-Kremenchuk-Kryvyi Rig' and its South-corridor classification ARE present in the extracted text (lines ~235, ~668 of the extraction), so I am citing it on that manual override, consistent with documented project practice. GulfPub's registered dataset (already ingested in this batch's recon-gulfpub-20260812) independently matches P0783 (composite 0.50, yellow) to a Naftogaz-sourced segment 'Romny - Kremenchuk' with diameter_in=56.0 (=1422mm, i.e. the same 1420mm pipe) and operator 'Naftogaz' — a THIRD, genuinely independent origin (Petroleum Economist World Map, scraped 2025-12-11, contact Oleksandr Khlyust @ Naftogaz) corroborating both the physical existence of a large-diameter (1420mm-class) trunk on this Romny–Kremenchuk stretch of the corridor and its classification as a Naftogaz/TSO-run transmission line, not a gathering/process line. Net: existence and transmission classification are corroborated by 3 independent origins (Naftogaz/Energy-Charter master plan via Wikipedia, energybase.ru's commercial infra database, and GulfPub's Naftogaz-sourced extract) — tier=high overall for existence/classification, even though not every individual cell below reaches that bar on its own.

validity.recommendation: flag for cluster-level adjudication, do not merge unilaterally — check P0783's Kremenchuk→Kryvyi Rih tail against P1460 (Dikanka-Kremenchuk-Kryvyi Rih, 700mm/272.2km) and P0783's Kremenchuk hub against P1485 (Kremenchuk-Anan'iv-Bohorodchany, 1020mm/532km)
validity.researcher_notes: P0783 shares its 'Kremenchuk' hub node with two other roster rows, and the physical-corridor evidence is genuinely ambiguous, not something I should resolve alone. (1) P1460 'Dikanka-Kremenchuk–Krivyi Rih Gas Pipeline' (len=272.2km, dia=700mm) has the IDENTICAL Kremenchuk→Kryvyi Rih tail segment as P0783 (len=771km total, dia=1420mm) but a different origin (Dykanka UGS, not Yelets/Russia) and a much smaller diameter. Wikipedia's list of 'main pipelines of the southern transit corridor' names Yelets–Kremenchuk–Kryvyi Rih, Shebelinka–Dnipropetrovsk–Kryvyi Rih–Rozdilna–Izmail, Kremenchuk–Ananyiv–Bohorodchany, Ananyiv–Tiraspol–Izmail, and Rozdilna–Izmail — a 'Dykanka–Kremenchuk–Kryvyi Rih' line is NOT among them, which is odd if it is a fully separate named trunk. The differing diameter (700mm vs 1420mm) argues against a straight duplicate (more likely a parallel smaller-bore line on the same corridor, which is normal Soviet practice — c.f. the legitimate parallel Ivatsevichy-Kobryn-Dolyna I/II pair), but the identical tail routing means GEM may be double-counting the same physical right-of-way as two 'pipelines' when it is actually one trunk plus a parallel/feeder line, or P1460 may itself be a mislabeled/duplicate entity. (2) GulfPub's reconciliation (recon-gulfpub-20260812/match_diff.json) independently flags a segment 'Kremenchuk - Ananyev' (321.9km) as AMBIGUOUS between P0783 and P1485 ('candidates': P0783 composite 0.498, P1485 composite 0.465) — i.e. the automated matcher cannot cleanly separate which GEM row that continuation past Kremenchuk belongs to, and neither candidate clears the accept threshold on its own. This is exactly the kind of hub-node ambiguity the sweep brief flags for hand adjudication (cf. the Dikanka/Dolyna-hub clusters called out in the country guidance) — surfacing it here rather than silently assuming either P0783's or P1460's stated 771km/272km don't overlap.

validity.recommendation: re-verify Capacity against a current TSOUA technical-capacity document; do not apply either figure yet
validity.researcher_notes: GEM Capacity = 95.00 mill.Sm3/day (→ 34.675 bcm/year on a 365-day basis). Two independent sources give a lower figure, and they roughly agree with EACH OTHER but not tightly with GEM: (a) Naftogaz/Energy Charter Secretariat Master Plan (2009), as quoted verbatim by Wikipedia: 'capacity of 32 billion cubic metres per year' for the pipeline's Ukrainian section → 32e9/365 = 87.67 mill.Sm3/day — 7.3 mill.Sm3/day (7.7%) below GEM. (b) GulfPub's Naftogaz-sourced 'Romny - Kremenchuk' segment matched to P0783: Capacity_mmcfd = 3300 MMcf/day → 3300 × 28,316.846 m3 = 93.45 mill.Sm3/day — only 1.55 mill.Sm3/day (1.6%) below GEM, i.e. much closer. So GEM's figure sits just above the GulfPub/Naftogaz-scrape number and more visibly above the 2009 master-plan number; none of the three are wildly apart (all in the 87.7–95.0 range) but they do not agree at the precision the sheet implies, and the master-plan figure specifically describes the 'Ukrainian section' whereas GEM's Capacity presumably describes the whole line — a plausible but unconfirmed reason for a gap. This is a real, unresolved spec disagreement (not large enough to suspect a wrong pipeline, but too large to silently pass) — flagging rather than picking a winner, per the corroboration rule.

validity.recommendation: Length is not independently pinned at the full 771 km (Yelets→Kryvyi Rih) scope; only the Ukrainian-section sub-length is sourced — leave as is but note the gap for a future pass
validity.researcher_notes: GEM LengthKnown = 771.00 km for the full Yelets(Russia)→Kryvyi Rih(Ukraine) route. The only hard length figure I found, Naftogaz/Energy Charter Master Plan via Wikipedia, is scoped only to the 'Ukrainian section' = 323 km — not directly comparable to GEM's binational total. Back-solving, 771 − 323 = 448 km implied for the Russian (Yelets→Sudzha-border) portion, which is geographically plausible (Yelets to the Sudzha border-crossing area is roughly 270–300 km airline distance; a buried trunk with realistic routing detours to ~440–450 km is normal, similar ratios hold for the Soyuz and Progress pipelines in the same Wikipedia table). I also tried to triangulate via GulfPub's finer city-to-city segmentation of the Ukrainian leg (Romny→Kremenchuk 239.8km + Kremenchuk→Radushnoe 135.2km + Radushnoe→Kryvyi Rih 17.7km = 392.7km) but that chain runs ~22% longer than the master-plan's 323km 'Ukrainian section' figure and most of those GulfPub sub-segments carry no diameter value (only the first, Romny–Kremenchuk, does, at 56in/1420mm) — meaning some of that chain is plausibly a smaller-diameter distribution branch feeding Kryvyi Rih's industrial users rather than a straight continuation of the 1420mm trunk, so I am NOT using that 392.7km sum as a check figure. Net: no source contradicts 771km, but no source confirms the total either — confirmed-with-caveat, not a hard conflict.

validity.recommendation: no action — the Russia/Ukraine ownership split already on the row is the structurally correct pattern for this cross-border trunk; a percentage-level source was not found
validity.researcher_notes: Owner1='Gazprom PJSC', Owner2='Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine', no percentages given. Per the country guidance, a row spanning Russia→Ukraine should show a SPLIT (Russian section under Gazprom, Ukrainian section under the Ukrainian state operator), not 100% Gazprom for a domestic Ukrainian asset — and that is exactly what this row already records, so there is no attribution error to fix here. energybase.ru's object page (unverifiable URL, see existence note) names the operating company as ООО «Газпром трансгаз Москва» (a Gazprom subsidiary) for the pipeline overall, consistent with Gazprom's role on the Russian section; it does not speak to the Ukrainian side. Since 1 Jan 2020 the Ukrainian GTS operator is TSOUA (Gas TSO of Ukraine, tsoua.com) rather than the pre-2020 Ukrtransgaz — 'Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine' as currently written is the right generic description of that entity. I could not find a citable public source giving the actual ownership percentage split, so I'm not proposing a ref for this cell; flagging only that the existing values look right in kind, just unsourced.
